claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for your child, I need to ask you a few questions.

**What is your child's name, and how old are they?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: My child's name is Alex, and they're 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 18 years old, their eligibility may depend on whether they're still in education or training.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** (For example, studying for A-levels, Scottish Highers, or similar qualifications at school or college)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - they're studying for their A-levels at college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Now I need to understand a bit more about your relationship to Alex and your living situation.

**Are you Alex's parent or the person responsible for them, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm Alex's parent and they live at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand your residency status.

**Are you currently living in the UK, and are you a UK resident (or do you have the right to reside in the UK)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to clarify your immigration or residency status a bit more.

**Are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another type of visa or immigration status that gives you the right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**When will Alex turn 19 years old?** (I need to know their date of birth or when they'll reach 19, as this affects how long Child Benefit can continue)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd need to check the exact date, but they'll be turning 19 later this year - they're currently 18.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That timing is important because Child Benefit usually stops on specific dates related to when a young person turns 19 and when their course ends.

One more question:

**When does Alex's A-level course end?** (For example, will they finish in May/June of this year, or does the course extend beyond their 19th birthday?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They'll be finishing their A-levels in June this year, so before they turn 19.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good News!

**You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 18 and studying for A-levels at college, which counts as full-time non-advanced education
- You're Alex's parent, they live with you, and you're responsible for them
- You're a UK citizen living in the UK
- Alex is still within the age range where Child Benefit can be claimed for young people in education (16-19)

**Important information about when the benefit will stop:**

Since Alex will finish their A-levels in June before turning 19, your Child Benefit for Alex will continue until either:
- The end of their course (June), OR
- The 31st August following when they leave education

This means you should continue to receive Child Benefit until at least the end of August this year.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit for Alex, you can make a claim now. If you're already receiving it, it should continue automatically as long as you've informed the Child Benefit Office that Alex is in education.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit entitlement?
